script.title: Why This Indian Coal Giant Is Raising ₹8,000 Cr #shorts

segments.text: A single Indian coal firm just launched an ₹8,000 crore IPO.
segments.broll: aerial wide shot open pit coal mine

segments.text: That is Mahanadi Coalfields, a massive subsidiary of government giant Coal India.
segments.broll: close up heavy cargo train coal

segments.text: But why does a profitable state-owned coal giant even need public money?
segments.broll: medium shot indian stock broker looking at screens
broll_alt: trader analyzing charts laptop close up
hand typing on laptop financial desk

segments.text: Parent companies list subsidiaries to unlock hidden value and fund green energy projects without heavy bank debt.
segments.broll: aerial solar panels field sunny day
broll_alt: green energy power plant wide shot

segments.text: Coal still powers over seventy percent of India's electricity, keeping demand booming.
segments.broll: wide shot thermal power plant smoke stacks night

segments.text: However, commodity profits fluctuate wildly whenever global market prices change.
segments.broll: close up hands holding rupee cash notes
broll_alt: counting indian currency notes close up
rupee money stack on office table

segments.text: Not financial advice, but always check real cash flows before chasing IPO hype, especially when...
